name: The SI second is a caesium hyperfine frequency
summary: Since 1967 the second has been defined by fixing the Cs ground-state hyperfine frequency. Time and frequency are the most precisely realised SI quantities, and the metre is traced to them through the fixed value of c.

name: Unitary Fermi gas: universality from a missing scale
summary: At a Feshbach resonance the scattering length diverges and drops out, leaving density as the only scale. Dimensional analysis then forces every observable to be a universal number times its free-Fermi-gas value, the Bertsch parameter ξ being one example. Dilute neutron matter shares the same universality.

name: AMO measurements determine α and m_e for CODATA
summary: The fine-structure constant comes from atom-recoil interferometry (h/m for Cs and Rb) and from the Penning-trap electron g-factor combined with QED. These AMO inputs dominate the CODATA values of α, R∞ and m_e, and the ~5σ gap between the Cs and Rb values remains unresolved.

name: Clock ratios test the constancy of α and m_p/m_e
summary: Different transitions depend on α and μ = m_p/m_e with different sensitivities, so repeated ratios between clocks (Al+/Hg+, Yb+ E3/E2, Cs/Sr) bound present-day drifts at the ~10^{-18} per year level. The same ratios search for ultralight dark matter, which would make the constants oscillate.
sources: Rosenband et al. (2008). "Frequency Ratio of Al+and Hg+Single-Ion Optical Clocks; Metrology at the 17th Decimal Place". *Science* 319, 1808. [doi:10.1126/science.1154622](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1154622)

name: Hydrogen spectroscopy, R∞ and the proton radius
summary: The Rydberg constant and the proton charge radius are fitted together to hydrogen and deuterium transition frequencies. The muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift (2010) gave a radius 4% smaller. The puzzle eased once newer hydrogen measurements and CODATA 2018/2022 moved to about 0.84 fm.

name: Optical clocks and redefining the second
summary: Optical lattice and ion clocks now beat the Cs primary standard by about 100×. The CIPM roadmap therefore plans an optical redefinition of the second around 2030, continuing the 2019 move to defining units by fixed constants.

name: Scientific computing toolkit powers numerical relativity
summary: Numerical relativity is a flagship application of large-scale scientific computing: adaptive mesh refinement, high-order finite-difference and multidomain spectral solvers, constraint damping and parallel HPC turned the Einstein equations into working codes, culminating in the 2005 binary-black-hole breakthrough.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: Machine learning for GW searches, glitches and inference
summary: Convolutional networks detect compact-binary signals and classify instrumental glitches (Gravity Spy), normalizing-flow simulation-based inference gives full posteriors in seconds, and ML surrogates of numerical-relativity waveforms speed up parameter estimation, complementing matched filtering and stochastic sampling.

name: MCMC and nested sampling for GW source parameters
summary: Posteriors over the ~15 parameters of a compact binary are sampled with Markov-chain Monte Carlo and nested sampling (LALInference, Bilby), direct descendants of the Metropolis algorithm; nested sampling also yields the Bayesian evidence used for model selection and tests of GR.
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Monte Carlo over geometries: causal dynamical triangulations
summary: Causal dynamical triangulations define the gravitational path integral as a sum over causal simplicial geometries, Wick-rotated and sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo as in lattice field theory; simulations find a phase with an extended de Sitter-like 4D geometry whose spectral dimension runs from ~4 at large scales to ~2 at short scales.

name: Well-posed hyperbolic formulations and PDE integrators
summary: The Einstein equations become a stable initial-value problem only in strongly hyperbolic formulations (generalized harmonic, BSSN with moving punctures); they are then evolved by method-of-lines Runge–Kutta with finite differences plus AMR or spectral methods, with constraint damping controlling constraint growth.
sources: Pretorius (2005). "Evolution of Binary Black-Hole Spacetimes". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 95, 121101. [arXiv:gr-qc/0507014](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0507014)

name: MERA and holographic codes as discrete AdS
summary: In a tensor network, a boundary region's entropy is bounded by the number of bonds a minimal cut crosses times log χ, a discrete Ryu–Takayanagi formula; MERA's renormalization direction resembles a hyperbolic slice of AdS (Swingle), and holographic codes built from perfect tensors model bulk reconstruction as quantum error correction.
breaks: Exact RT behaviour holds only for special (stabilizer or random) networks with flat entanglement spectra; there is no sub-AdS locality or Einstein dynamics, and MERA's emergent geometry has been argued to be closer to de Sitter or light-cone than to a spatial AdS slice.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Hole argument and the meaning of general covariance
summary: Einstein's 1913 hole argument, in which diffeomorphism-related solutions agree outside a region but differ inside it, seemed to make generally covariant field equations indeterministic; its resolution (spacetime points have no identity apart from the metric) let Einstein accept general covariance in 1915 and started the modern substantivalism–relationism debate.

name: Problem of time in canonical quantum gravity
summary: Canonical quantization of GR gives a Hamiltonian constraint (the Wheeler–DeWitt equation) with no external time, the 'frozen formalism'; loop quantum gravity and philosophy of physics both face the task of defining dynamics through relational observables and of saying what change means in a timeless theory.

name: GR as a showcase of mathematical-physics methods
summary: GR brings many mathematical methods together: the Einstein equations as a constrained nonlinear hyperbolic PDE system, Green's-function solutions of linearized gravity, perturbation expansions (post-Newtonian, black-hole perturbation theory) and spin-weighted spherical harmonics for radiation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Euclidean periodicity fixes the Hawking temperature
summary: Wick-rotating the Schwarzschild metric gives a smooth Euclidean geometry only if imaginary time is periodic with period 2πc/κ; since thermal Green's functions are periodic in imaginary time (KMS condition), that period is ħ/k_BT, which is the Hawking temperature (Gibbons–Hawking).
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Ringdown quasinormal modes as Green's-function poles
summary: Black-hole ringdown is a sum of quasinormal modes: complex frequencies at the poles of the perturbation Green's function in the lower half ω-plane (plus a branch cut that gives late-time tails), computed by Leaver's continued fractions or WKB; they depend only on mass and spin, which enables black-hole spectroscopy.

name: String worldsheets as Riemann surfaces
summary: Perturbative string amplitudes are integrals over moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces; worldsheet conformal invariance makes the theory a 2D CFT, worked with holomorphic functions, contour-integral operator product expansions and modular invariance of the torus amplitude.

name: Retarded Green's function yields the quadrupole formula
summary: In Lorenz gauge, linearized gravity is a sourced wave equation for the trace-reversed perturbation; the same retarded Green's function as in electrodynamics gives the far-zone field and hence the quadrupole formula for gravitational radiation.
sources: Blanchet (2014; updated 2024). "Post-Newtonian Theory for Gravitational Waves". *Living Rev. Relativ.* [arXiv:1310.1528](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.1528)

name: Random-subsystem entropy gives the Page curve
summary: Averaging subsystem entanglement entropy over Haar-random pure states in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space gives nearly maximal entropy for the smaller factor; applied to a black hole plus its radiation, this gives the Page curve (radiation entropy rises, then falls after the Page time), which unitarity requires and Hawking's calculation misses.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

name: Singularity theorems and global causal structure
summary: Global Lorentzian geometry (the Raychaudhuri focusing equation, trapped surfaces, conformal compactification into Penrose diagrams) proves that a trapped surface plus an energy condition implies geodesic incompleteness, so black-hole singularities are generic rather than artifacts of symmetry.
sources: Penrose (1965). "Gravitational Collapse and Space-Time Singularities". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 14, 57. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.14.57)

name: Lorentzian geometry is the language of gravity
summary: GR models gravity as curvature of a Lorentzian manifold: free fall is geodesic motion, the equivalence principle is local flatness in normal coordinates, and tidal forces are the Riemann tensor acting through geodesic deviation.
sources: Einstein (1916). "Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativitätstheorie". *Ann. Phys.* 354, 769. [doi:10.1002/andp.19163540702](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19163540702)

name: Contracted Bianchi identity fixes the Einstein tensor
summary: The contracted Bianchi identity makes the Einstein tensor identically divergence-free, so it can consistently be set equal to a conserved stress–energy tensor; the field equations are a statement in Riemannian geometry about Ricci curvature.

name: Petrov classification and algebraically special metrics
summary: Classifying the Weyl tensor by its principal null directions (Petrov types, Newman–Penrose formalism) organizes the exact solutions; Kerr found the rotating black hole by searching for algebraically special vacuum metrics, and the Goldberg–Sachs theorem links that degeneracy to shear-free null congruences.
sources: Kerr (1963). "Gravitational Field of a Spinning Mass as an Example of Algebraically Special Metrics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 11, 237. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.11.237)

name: Lovelock's theorem defines the routes to modified gravity
summary: In four dimensions the only symmetric, divergence-free rank-2 tensor built from the metric and its first two derivatives is a combination of G_μν and g_μν; every modified-gravity theory escapes this by adding fields (scalar-tensor, Horndeski), higher derivatives (f(R)), extra dimensions or nonlocality.

name: Template-bank metric on the waveform manifold
summary: The fractional SNR lost between neighbouring templates defines a Riemannian metric on source-parameter space, and template banks are lattices laid out with this metric; the related Fisher information matrix gives forecast parameter uncertainties.

name: Ashtekar connection variables recast GR as gauge theory
summary: Rewriting canonical GR with an SU(2) connection and a densitized triad (Ashtekar, later Ashtekar–Barbero) gives it a Yang–Mills-like phase space; holonomies of the connection and fluxes of the triad are the basic variables quantized in loop quantum gravity.
sources: Ashtekar (1986). "New Variables for Classical and Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 2244. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.57.2244)

name: Lorentz transformations as isometries of Minkowski metric
summary: Minkowski's reformulation makes Lorentz transformations the isometries of a flat metric of Lorentzian signature; four-vectors and tensors make laws manifestly covariant, and GR reuses the same machinery for curved metrics.
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: VLBI: heterodyne receivers, maser clocks and correlators
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope is an Earth-sized interferometer: each station down-converts 1.3 mm signals with heterodyne receivers and time-stamps them with hydrogen-maser clocks, and correlators combine the recordings into visibilities whose diffraction limit resolves the ~40 μas ring; imaging is then an ill-posed inverse problem solved with regularized and Bayesian methods.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Standard quantum limit and squeezed light in GW detectors
summary: Interferometric GW detectors are limited by fundamental instrument noise: photon shot noise and radiation-pressure noise combine into the standard quantum limit, thermal noise follows the fluctuation–dissipation theorem, and injecting squeezed vacuum (frequency-dependent since O4) beats the shot-noise limit.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Matched filtering and Bayesian inference of GW signals
summary: GW detection is a likelihood-ratio test built on a noise-weighted inner product (matched filtering against template banks); significance comes from time-slide background estimation, and source parameters from Bayesian posteriors.
sources: LIGO Scientific and Virgo Collaborations (2016). "Observation of Gravitational Waves from a Binary Black Hole Merger". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 061102. [arXiv:1602.03837](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.03837)

name: Hellings–Downs correlation and Bayesian evidence in PTAs
summary: A stochastic GW background makes timing residuals correlated between pulsar pairs according to the Hellings–Downs curve; PTA collaborations weigh evidence for it with Bayes factors and frequentist statistics against common-spectrum red noise, reaching ~3–4σ significance in 2023.
sources: NANOGrav Collaboration (2023). "The NANOGrav 15 yr Data Set: Evidence for a Gravitational-wave Background". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 951, L8. [arXiv:2306.16213](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.16213)

name: CPT tests double as Lorentz-invariance tests
summary: The CPT theorem follows from Lorentz invariance plus locality, and in local interacting QFT CPT violation implies Lorentz violation; so kaon mass differences, antihydrogen spectroscopy and Penning-trap particle–antiparticle comparisons constrain Lorentz-violating coefficients of the Standard-Model Extension.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: AdS isometries equal the boundary conformal group
summary: The isometry group of AdS_{d+1} is SO(d,2), exactly the conformal group of d-dimensional Minkowski space (extended to PSU(2,2|4) for AdS5×S5 and N=4 SYM); this symmetry match underlies the bulk-field/boundary-operator dictionary, where bulk mass fixes the operator's scaling dimension.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)
Witten (1998). "Anti De Sitter Space And Holography". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 253. [arXiv:hep-th/9802150](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9802150)

name: SU(2) spin networks and the quantized area spectrum
summary: LQG states are spin networks, graphs whose edges carry SU(2) irreducible representations j and whose nodes carry intertwiners; the area operator is diagonal on them with eigenvalues fixed by the SU(2) Casimir, so area is discrete.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1995). "Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 442, 593. [arXiv:gr-qc/9411005](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005)

name: Special relativity is Poincaré invariance
summary: Special relativity says physics is invariant under the Poincaré group; Wigner's unitary irreducible representations classify particles by mass and spin, and the double cover SL(2,C) of the Lorentz group gives spinors.
map: SO^+(1,3)\cong SL(2,\mathbb C)/\mathbb Z_2,\quad P^\mu P_\mu=-m^2c^2\ (\text{Casimir})
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)

name: Killing symmetries give conserved orbital constants
summary: Each Killing vector of a black-hole metric gives a quantity conserved along geodesics (energy from ∂_t, angular momentum from ∂_φ), and Komar integrals define mass and spin; Kerr also has a Killing tensor that gives the Carter constant, a hidden symmetry that makes geodesic motion integrable.

name: Diffeomorphism invariance gives local conservation
summary: Diffeomorphism invariance of the matter action implies covariant conservation of the stress–energy tensor, and invariance of the Einstein–Hilbert action implies the Bianchi identity (Noether's second theorem); globally conserved energy exists only with Killing vectors or asymptotic symmetries.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: No local gravitational energy; GW energy as averaged or boundary charge
summary: Because diffeomorphisms are a local gauge symmetry, Noether's second theorem gives no gauge-invariant local energy density for gravity; GW energy is defined only by averaging over wavelengths (Isaacson tensor) or as charges at null infinity, where the Bondi mass decreases as waves escape and BMS supertranslation charges are tied to the gravitational memory effect.
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)

name: Spontaneous Lorentz violation in the SME
summary: Lorentz symmetry could break spontaneously, with a vector or tensor field acquiring a vacuum expectation value that picks out a frame (Kostelecký–Samuel, bumblebee models); the Standard-Model Extension parametrizes the resulting background coefficients, and the associated Nambu–Goldstone modes have been proposed as photons or gravitons.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: Scale-free vacuum GR: one simulation serves all masses
summary: The vacuum Einstein equations have no intrinsic length scale, so binary-black-hole simulations are run in units of total mass M and rescale to any mass: times and lengths scale as GM/c^3 and GM/c^2, and strain is (GM/c^2)/D times a universal function. Matter breaks this scaling, which is why neutron-star mergers must be simulated separately for each equation of state.
map: t\to\lambda t,\ x\to\lambda x,\ M\to\lambda M:\quad f_{\rm GW}\propto\frac{c^3}{GM},\ h\propto\frac{GM}{c^2D}

name: Constancy of constants tests the equivalence principle
summary: Local position invariance, part of the Einstein equivalence principle, requires dimensionless constants such as α and m_p/m_e to be the same everywhere and at all times; atomic-clock comparisons, the Oklo natural reactor and quasar spectra bound their drift, and any variation would generically also violate the weak equivalence principle.
sources: Will (2014). "The Confrontation between General Relativity and Experiment". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 17, 4. [arXiv:1403.7377](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.7377)

name: Black-hole entropy is horizon area in Planck units
summary: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is a quarter of the horizon area counted in Planck areas, and the Hawking temperature combines ħ, c, G and k_B; it is the clearest formula in which all four constants appear together, which is why black holes serve as a quantum-gravity laboratory.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Planck scale marks where quantum gravity is order one
summary: Combining G, ħ and c gives the Planck length, time and energy, where gravitational and quantum effects are both order one; every quantum-gravity programme is organized around this scale, and its ~10^15 gap above LHC energies is why direct tests are so hard.

name: Planck-suppressed dispersion and GRB time-of-flight bounds
summary: If quantum gravity changes photon dispersion at order E/E_P, high-energy photons from distant gamma-ray bursts arrive with energy-dependent delays proportional to E/E_P times the light-travel time; Fermi-LAT timing of GRB 090510 pushed the linear-order scale beyond E_P, so the Planck scale itself is now an experimentally probed quantity.
sources: Mattingly (2005). "Modern Tests of Lorentz Invariance". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 8, 5. [arXiv:gr-qc/0502097](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0502097)

name: SI second as proper time; relativistic geodesy
summary: The SI second is a proper time realized by clocks, so International Atomic Time is referred to an equipotential surface and corrected for gravitational redshift; optical clocks now resolve centimetre height differences, which turns the GR redshift into a geodesy tool and a requirement for any optical redefinition of the second.
sources: Pound & Rebka (1960). "Apparent Weight of Photons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 4, 337. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.4.337)

name: Lattice QCD as a computational-physics workload
summary: Lattice field theory turns the Euclidean path integral into a very high-dimensional integral attacked with the whole computational toolkit: Markov-chain Monte Carlo, Krylov and multigrid solvers for the Dirac operator, and now ML samplers and tensor networks. Lattice QCD has in turn driven dedicated supercomputer design (APE, QCDOC).
sources: Wilson (1974). "Confinement of quarks". *Phys. Rev. D* 10, 2445. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.10.2445)

name: Neural tools shared by physics and HEP
summary: The same neural tools (classifiers, generative surrogates, normalizing flows, graph networks, anomaly detectors) serve physics in general and HEP in particular. In HEP they tag jets, emulate calorimeter showers, run in triggers and power simulation-based inference, and HEP was an early adopter and a main source of benchmark datasets.
sources: Carleo et al. (2019). "Machine learning and the physical sciences". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 91, 045002. [arXiv:1903.10563](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10563)

name: Hybrid Monte Carlo: molecular dynamics in fictitious time
summary: HMC samples lattice gauge fields with dynamical fermions by adding conjugate momenta, integrating Hamilton's equations with a reversible, volume-preserving leapfrog or Omelyan integrator, and removing the integration error with a Metropolis step. It was invented for lattice QCD and later adopted in Bayesian statistics (NUTS in Stan).

name: Event generators as Monte Carlo integrators
summary: Event generators do importance-sampled (VEGAS-type adaptive) phase-space integration of factorized cross sections, hit-or-miss unweighting into events, and parton showers sampled with the veto algorithm. The shower samples the Sudakov no-emission probability with the same survival-probability logic used to sample radioactive decay times.

name: Euclidean action as a Boltzmann weight
summary: After Wick rotation, e^{iS} becomes e^{-S_E}, so lattice QFT is a statistical-mechanics problem sampled by Markov-chain Monte Carlo (heat bath, HMC). It inherits that field's problems: autocorrelation, critical slowing down toward the continuum limit, and the sign problem when the weight is not positive.
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

name: Tensor networks for lattice gauge theories
summary: In the Hamiltonian formulation, MPS and DMRG simulate 1+1D lattice gauge theories such as the Schwinger model without importance sampling, so they avoid the sign problem at finite density, with a θ term and in real time. Gauss's law can be built into gauge-invariant tensors, and these results benchmark quantum simulators of gauge theories.
sources: Schollwöck (2011). "The density-matrix renormalization group in the age of matrix product states". *Ann. Phys.* 326, 96. [arXiv:1008.3477](https://arxiv.org/abs/1008.3477)

name: Particle physics as the archetype of big science
summary: The path from cosmic-ray and accelerator discoveries to the Standard Model is a central case study in the history of physics. The field also defined 'big science': Lawrence's cyclotron laboratory, CERN (1954) as a model of international collaboration, and LHC collaborations with thousands of authors.

name: Naturalness as an argument form
summary: The hierarchy problem rests on naturalness, a fine-tuning argument that philosophy of physics studies as a heuristic. Its past success (the charm-quark mass estimated from K⁰ mixing) and the LHC's null searches for natural new physics have made its epistemic status an open debate.

name: Dispersive hadronic vacuum polarization for muon g−2
summary: Analyticity and the optical theorem turn the measured e⁺e⁻→hadrons cross section into the leading hadronic contribution to the muon g−2 through a Kramers–Kronig-type integral. Tensions among the e⁺e⁻ data sets (CMD-3 versus earlier experiments) and with lattice QCD are why this term decides the Standard Model comparison.

name: Holomorphy and the Virasoro algebra in 2D CFT
summary: In two dimensions the conformal maps are exactly the holomorphic functions, so the stress tensor splits into T(z) and T̄(z̄). Radial quantization turns charges into contour integrals, Ward identities and operator-product expansions follow from the residue theorem, and the Virasoro generators are Laurent coefficients.

name: S-matrix analyticity, dispersion relations and cuts
summary: Causality makes scattering amplitudes analytic in the energy variables, so they obey dispersion relations, the relativistic version of Kramers–Kronig. The optical theorem and Cutkosky rules give the discontinuities across branch cuts, and the modern unitarity method rebuilds loop amplitudes from their cuts.
map: \mathcal M(s)=\frac1\pi\int_{s_0}^\infty ds'\frac{\mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal M(s')}{s'-s-i\epsilon},\ \mathrm{Im}\,\mathcal M(s,0)=2E_{\rm cm}p_{\rm cm}\sigma_{\rm tot}

name: The Feynman propagator is a Green's function
summary: The propagator is the Green's function of the Klein–Gordon (or Dirac) operator, with the iε prescription choosing time-ordered boundary conditions, so the Feynman-diagram expansion is a Born series in Green's functions. Differential equations in the kinematic variables are also a main tool for evaluating loop integrals.
sources: Feynman (1949). "Space-Time Approach to Quantum Electrodynamics". *Phys. Rev.* 76, 769. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.76.769](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.76.769)

name: Neutrino mixing as a unitary basis change
summary: Flavour and mass eigenstates are related by the unitary PMNS matrix, so oscillation is the time evolution of a superposition of energy eigenstates. The two-flavour formula is the two-level Rabi formula, and the MSW effect is adiabatic passage through an avoided crossing of the matter Hamiltonian's eigenvalues.
sources: Wolfenstein (1978). "Neutrino oscillations in matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 17, 2369. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.17.2369)

name: CKM matrix from bi-unitary diagonalization of Yukawas
summary: Quark mass matrices are diagonalized by separate left and right unitary rotations (a singular-value decomposition), and the CKM matrix is the mismatch between the up- and down-type left rotations. Parameter counting leaves (n−1)(n−2)/2 CP phases, one for three generations, and the Jarlskog invariant measures it independently of basis.
sources: Kobayashi & Maskawa (1973). "CP-Violation in the Renormalizable Theory of Weak Interaction". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 49, 652. [doi:10.1143/PTP.49.652](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.49.652)

name: Instanton number as a Chern class; index theorem
summary: Instantons are classified by the second Chern (Pontryagin) number of the gauge bundle, and the θ term integrates that characteristic class. The Atiyah–Singer index theorem ties it to the Dirac operator's zero modes, which is the topological content of the axial anomaly.

name: Gauge fields as connections, field strength as curvature
summary: A gauge potential is a connection on a principal bundle and the field strength is its curvature, the same structures as the spin connection and Riemann tensor of general relativity. Wilson loops are holonomies, and a Bianchi identity holds in both.
breaks: The gravitational connection is soldered to the tangent bundle and fixed by the metric; internal gauge connections live on an abstract bundle with no metric to determine them.
sources: Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Collider physics as measurement at scale
summary: Collider experiments use the full measurement chain: calibration, unfolding of detector response, systematic uncertainties as nuisance parameters, and blind analyses. HEP also produced much of the statistics toolkit physicists now share (Feldman–Cousins intervals, CLs, asymptotic profile-likelihood formulae).
sources: Feldman & Cousins (1998). "Unified approach to the classical statistical analysis of small signals". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 3873. [arXiv:physics/9711021](https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/9711021)
Read (2002). "Presentation of search results: the CLs technique". *J. Phys. G* 28, 2693. [doi:10.1088/0954-3899/28/10/313](https://doi.org/10.1088/0954-3899/28/10/313)

name: Axion haloscopes at the quantum noise limit
summary: Haloscopes such as ADMX convert dark-matter axions into microwave photons in a magnetized cavity, and the ~10⁻²² W signal makes the scan rate scale as 1/T_sys². Josephson parametric amplifiers at the standard quantum limit, squeezed states (HAYSTAC) and qubit-based photon counting are the enabling detector physics.

name: Calibration chains and resolution in collider experiments
summary: Collider experiments apply instrumentation principles at scale: test-beam and in-situ calibration with Z→ee and J/ψ resonances, luminosity from van der Meer beam-separation scans, and electronics noise and pile-up as limits on energy resolution.

name: Shared signal chain: sensors, preamps and noise
summary: In a particle detector, ionization or light becomes charge, which charge-sensitive preamplifiers amplify and shape, with thermal and shot noise setting the equivalent noise charge. Photomultipliers, SiPMs and silicon sensors are common to both nodes, and triggers are real-time filters working under bandwidth limits.

name: Profile likelihood, CLs and the 5σ discovery rule
summary: LHC searches are hypothesis tests: profile-likelihood ratios with systematics as nuisance parameters, Wilks/Wald asymptotics giving Z = √q₀, CLs for exclusions, and look-elsewhere corrections, as used in the 2012 Higgs discovery.
sources: Cowan, Cranmer, Gross & Vitells (2011). "Asymptotic formulae for likelihood-based tests of new physics". *Eur. Phys. J. C* 71, 1554. [arXiv:1007.1727](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.1727)

ATLAS Collaboration (2012). "Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC". *Phys. Lett. B* 716, 1. [arXiv:1207.7214](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.7214)

name: Simulation-based inference and the likelihood-ratio trick
summary: When a simulator yields samples but no tractable likelihood, a classifier trained to separate θ₀ samples from θ₁ samples estimates the likelihood ratio, which by Neyman–Pearson is the optimal test statistic. Neural likelihood-ratio and posterior estimation now replace binned histogram fits in some ATLAS measurements.

name: Judging anomalies: systematics and correlated errors
summary: Whether an anomaly is real depends on its uncertainty budget. The muon g−2 comparison turned on the hadronic-vacuum-polarization error (mutually inconsistent e⁺e⁻ data versus lattice QCD, whose 2025 consensus value agrees with experiment), and the CDF W-mass outlier is a case study in combining correlated systematics across experiments.

name: The Standard Model as representation theory
summary: The Standard Model is defined by its gauge group SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) and by assigning each field to an irreducible representation, while Wigner's unitary Poincaré irreps label particles by mass and spin. Charges, multiplets and allowed couplings follow from group theory.
sources: Wigner (1939). "On Unitary Representations of the Inhomogeneous Lorentz Group". *Ann. Math.* 40, 149. [doi:10.2307/1968551](https://doi.org/10.2307/1968551)
Glashow (1961). "Partial-symmetries of weak interactions". *Nucl. Phys.* 22, 579. [doi:10.1016/0029-5582(61)90469-2](https://doi.org/10.1016/0029-5582(61)90469-2)

name: Strong CP problem and the Peccei–Quinn axion
summary: The QCD θ term is P- and T-odd and would give the neutron an electric dipole moment; the bound |d_n| < 1.8×10⁻²⁶ e cm forces |θ̄| ≲ 10⁻¹⁰. The Peccei–Quinn solution makes θ̄ dynamical: the axion, a pseudo-Goldstone boson, relaxes it to zero.
sources: Peccei & Quinn (1977). "CP Conservation in the Presence of Pseudoparticles". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 38, 1440. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.38.1440)
Wilczek (1978). "Problem of Strong P and T Invariance in the Presence of Instantons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 40, 279. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.40.279)

name: CP violation and the CPT theorem
summary: CP violation in kaons and B mesons is the experimental side of discrete-symmetry theory, and by the CPT theorem it implies T violation, since observed directly in both systems. With three generations the CKM matrix carries exactly one physical CP phase.
sources: Kobayashi & Maskawa (1973). "CP-Violation in the Renormalizable Theory of Weak Interaction". *Prog. Theor. Phys.* 49, 652. [doi:10.1143/PTP.49.652](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.49.652)

name: Parity violation built into chiral SU(2)_L
summary: Lee and Yang's 1956 proposal and Wu's 1957 cobalt-60 experiment showed that the weak interaction violates parity maximally. Electroweak theory encodes this by putting only left-handed fermions in SU(2)_L doublets (V−A currents), so the gauge representations themselves break P and C, while CP survives up to the CKM phase.
sources: Lee & Yang (1956). "Question of Parity Conservation in Weak Interactions". *Phys. Rev.* 104, 254. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.104.254](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.104.254)
Wu et al. (1957). "Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay". *Phys. Rev.* 105, 1413. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.105.1413)

name: SU(5) and SO(10) embeddings of the Standard Model
summary: Grand unification is a group-embedding problem: SU(5) ⊃ SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1) fits one generation into 5̄ ⊕ 10, and SO(10) fits it into a single 16 that includes ν_R. The embedding quantizes hypercharge and fixes sin²θ_W = 3/8 at the unification scale.
sources: Georgi & Glashow (1974). "Unity of All Elementary-Particle Forces". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 32, 438. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.32.438)

name: Graded Lie algebras evade Coleman–Mandula
summary: Coleman–Mandula rules out any Lie-group symmetry of the S-matrix that mixes spacetime and internal symmetries non-trivially. Haag–Łopuszański–Sohnius showed that the only loophole is a graded algebra with fermionic generators, which is supersymmetry, whose anticommutator closes on the momentum.
sources: Martin (1997). "A Supersymmetry Primer". [arXiv:hep-ph/9709356](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9709356)

name: Flavour SU(3) multiplets and colour singlets
summary: The eightfold way sorts hadrons into flavour-SU(3) octets and decuplets, and the Gell-Mann–Okubo mass formula predicted the Ω⁻. The quark model reads hadrons as colour singlets in tensor products of 3 and 3̄, and the same products list the allowed tetraquark and pentaquark structures.

name: SU(3) colour Casimirs set QCD dynamics
summary: Quarks sit in the fundamental and gluons in the adjoint of SU(3), and the group invariants C_F = 4/3, C_A = 3 and T_F = 1/2 fix the β-function, the splitting functions and the colour factors. Gluon self-coupling through the non-abelian structure constants gives asymptotic freedom, and large-N_c expansions treat N as a parameter.
sources: Gross & Wilczek (1973). "Ultraviolet Behavior of Non-Abelian Gauge Theories". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1343. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343)
Politzer (1973). "Reliable Perturbative Results for Strong Interactions?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 30, 1346. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1346)

name: Anomalies: Noether currents broken by quantization
summary: A classically conserved Noether current can gain a nonzero divergence from the path-integral measure. The axial anomaly explains π⁰→γγ, and its coefficient is topological: exact at one loop (Adler–Bardeen) and protected from further corrections.

name: Gauging a Noether symmetry; Ward identities
summary: Making a global symmetry local forces in a gauge field that couples to the Noether current, and Noether's second theorem says local symmetries give identities rather than new charges. In quantum theory these become the Ward–Takahashi and Slavnov–Taylor identities, which protect charge universality and renormalizability.
map: \mathcal L\supset-eA_\mu j^\mu,\ \partial_\mu j^\mu=0\Rightarrow k_\mu\mathcal M^\mu(k)=0,\ Z_1=Z_2
sources: Noether (1918; English translation 1971). "Invariant variation problems". *Transport Theory Stat. Phys.* 1, 186. [doi:10.1080/00411457108231446](https://doi.org/10.1080/00411457108231446)
Yang & Mills (1954). "Conservation of Isotopic Spin and Isotopic Gauge Invariance". *Phys. Rev.* 96, 191. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.96.191](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.96.191)

name: Higgs boson as the amplitude mode of electroweak breaking
summary: A Mexican-hat potential gives the Higgs doublet a vacuum value v = 246 GeV that breaks SU(2)×U(1) to U(1)_em, and three would-be Goldstones become the longitudinal W and Z (Higgs–Anderson mechanism). The leftover custodial SU(2) gives ρ = 1 at tree level, and the Higgs boson is the radial (amplitude) mode.
sources: Englert & Brout (1964). "Broken Symmetry and the Mass of Gauge Vector Mesons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 321. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.321)
Higgs (1964). "Broken Symmetries and the Masses of Gauge Bosons". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 13, 508. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.13.508)

name: Chiral symmetry breaking: pions as pseudo-Goldstones
summary: The quark condensate breaks SU(2)_L×SU(2)_R to SU(2)_V, so pions are pseudo-Goldstone bosons, light because quark masses break the symmetry explicitly. This is Nambu's superconductivity analogy carried into hadron physics, and chiral perturbation theory is its low-energy effective theory.
sources: Nambu (1960). "Quasi-Particles and Gauge Invariance in the Theory of Superconductivity". *Phys. Rev.* 117, 648. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.117.648](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.117.648)
Goldstone (1961). "Field theories with Superconductor solutions". *Nuovo Cimento* 19, 154. [doi:10.1007/BF02812722](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02812722)

name: Anomalous dimensions and dimensional transmutation
summary: Quantum loops break naive dimensional analysis: because a renormalization scale μ enters, correlators scale with the engineering dimension plus an anomalous dimension, a case of Barenblatt's incomplete similarity. Classically scale-free QCD likewise generates Λ_QCD, a few hundred MeV, from a dimensionless coupling.
sources: Wilson & Kogut (1974). "The renormalization group and the ε expansion". *Phys. Rep.* 12, 75. [doi:10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-1573(74)90023-4)

name: Electron g−2, the fine-structure constant and muon g−2
summary: With five-loop QED, the electron g−2 gives α to sub-ppb precision, but the two atom-recoil values of α (Cs 2018, Rb 2020) disagree by more than 5σ, which limits that test of QED. The muon g−2 then tests the whole Standard Model, hadronic loops included.
sources: Morel et al. (2020). "Determination of the fine-structure constant with an accuracy of 81 parts per trillion". *Nature* 588, 61. [doi:10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-2964-7)

name: The fine-structure constant runs
summary: CODATA's α⁻¹ = 137.035999177 is the Thomson-limit value of a running coupling: vacuum polarization raises α to about 1/128.9 at the Z mass, and the hadronic part of that running comes from a dispersion integral over e⁺e⁻ data. A 'constant' of this kind is a renormalized coupling quoted at a stated scale.

name: Natural units and mass-dimension power counting
summary: With ħ = c = 1, particle physics measures everything in powers of energy and converts back through ħc. The mass dimension of fields and couplings then decides renormalizability, and a coupling of negative dimension, such as G_F = 1.1663787×10⁻⁵ GeV⁻², signals a heavier scale.

name: Planck scale vs weak scale: the hierarchy
summary: Natural units turn the hierarchy problem into a ratio of scales, M_Pl = √(ħc/G) ≈ 1.22×10¹⁹ GeV against v = 246 GeV. Large extra dimensions (ADD) lower the fundamental gravity scale to the TeV range by diluting gravity over a volume, while a warped extra dimension (RS) produces the ratio as an exponential.
map: M_{\rm Pl}^2\sim M_*^{n+2}R^n,\ m_{\rm weak}\sim e^{-k\pi r_c}M_{\rm Pl}
sources: Arkani-Hamed, Dimopoulos & Dvali (1998). "The hierarchy problem and new dimensions at a millimeter". *Phys. Lett. B* 429, 263. [arXiv:hep-ph/9803315](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9803315)
Randall & Sundrum (1999). "Large Mass Hierarchy from a Small Extra Dimension". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 83, 3370. [arXiv:hep-ph/9905221](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9905221)

name: Emulators and neural-network states for nuclear theory
summary: Eigenvector continuation and other reduced-basis emulators make Bayesian calibration of ab initio models affordable, and neural-network quantum states and NN-extrapolated no-core shell-model energies bring machine learning into the nuclear many-body problem.
breaks: Emulators interpolate within the training region and can fail where the ground state changes character.
sources: Frame et al. (2018). "Eigenvector Continuation with Subspace Learning". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 121, 032501. [arXiv:1711.07090](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.07090)
Wolfgruber et al. (2024). "Precise neural network predictions of energies and radii from the no-core shell model". *Phys. Rev. C* 110, 014327. [arXiv:2310.05256](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.05256)

name: Molecular dynamics of nuclear pasta and crust
summary: Classical and quantum molecular dynamics with screened-Coulomb plus nuclear potentials simulate millions of nucleons to find pasta shapes, defects, crust breaking strain and transport coefficients.
breaks: Semiclassical potentials miss shell effects and quantum degeneracy that can change pasta phase boundaries.
sources: Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Monte Carlo was invented for neutron transport
summary: Ulam, von Neumann and Metropolis created the Monte Carlo method in 1946-49 to follow neutron chains in fissile assemblies; today MC neutron transport (MCNP, Serpent, OpenMC) computes reactor k_eff and the Metropolis algorithm spread across physics.
map: k_{\rm eff}=\frac{N_{\rm gen+1}}{N_{\rm gen}};\ p(s)=\Sigma_te^{-\Sigma_ts}\Rightarrow s=-\frac{\ln\xi}{\Sigma_t}
sources: Metropolis et al. (1953). "Equation of State Calculations by Fast Computing Machines". *J. Chem. Phys.* 21, 1087. [doi:10.1063/1.1699114](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1699114)

name: Monte Carlo radiation transport for detectors and dose
summary: Detector response, shielding and dose are computed with Monte Carlo transport of photons, electrons, neutrons and ions (Geant4, FLUKA, MCNP), sampling interaction cross sections particle by particle.
breaks: Accuracy is limited by cross-section data and condensed-history approximations for charged particles.
sources: Agostinelli et al. (2003). "Geant4—a simulation toolkit". *Nucl. Instrum. Methods A* 506, 250. [doi:10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0168-9002(03)01368-8)

name: Monte Carlo jet-quenching event generators
summary: Medium-modified parton showers (JEWEL, MARTINI, MATTER/LBT in JETSCAPE) sample in-medium splitting and scattering stochastically inside an evolving QGP, extending collider event generators to heavy-ion jets.
breaks: Medium response and quantum interference (LPM) effects are implemented approximately and differ between generators.
sources: Cao et al. (2025). "Jet quenching: From theory to simulation". *Rep. Prog. Phys.*. [arXiv:2401.10026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10026)

name: Quantum Monte Carlo for nuclei
summary: Variational and Green's-function Monte Carlo and auxiliary-field diffusion Monte Carlo solve light nuclei and neutron matter by stochastic projection in imaginary time, sampling spin-isospin and spatial configurations.
breaks: The fermion sign problem forces constrained-path or fixed-node approximations as A grows.
sources: Carlson et al. (2015). "Quantum Monte Carlo methods for nuclear physics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 1067. [arXiv:1412.3081](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.3081)

name: Shock-capturing solvers for relativistic hydrodynamics
summary: Heavy-ion hydrodynamics codes (MUSIC and others) solve second-order viscous relativistic hydro with finite-volume, Kurganov-Tadmor shock-capturing schemes shared with astrophysical and numerical relativity codes.
breaks: Viscous relativistic hydro needs Israel-Stewart-type relaxation equations to remain causal, beyond standard conservation-law solvers.
sources: Schenke, Jeon & Gale (2010). "(3+1)D hydrodynamic simulation of relativistic heavy-ion collisions". *Phys. Rev. C* 82, 014903. [arXiv:1004.1408](https://arxiv.org/abs/1004.1408)

name: Entanglement and DMRG in the nuclear shell model
summary: Mode entanglement between proton and neutron orbitals is low in many nuclei, which motivates DMRG and tensor-network truncations of shell-model spaces and entanglement-guided orbital ordering borrowed from quantum chemistry.
breaks: Nuclear orbitals have no natural 1D ordering and long-range quadrupole correlations raise entanglement, so DMRG gains are smaller than in 1D lattices.
sources: Pérez-Obiol et al. (2023). "Quantum entanglement patterns in the structure of atomic nuclei within the nuclear shell model". *Eur. Phys. J. A* 59, 240. [arXiv:2307.05197](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.05197)

name: Fission and the birth of big science
summary: The 1938-39 discovery and interpretation of fission (Hahn, Strassmann, Meitner, Frisch) led within six years to reactors and weapons, the Manhattan Project and the national-laboratory system that reshaped how physics is organized and funded.
sources: Meitner & Frisch (1939). "Disintegration of Uranium by Neutrons: a New Type of Nuclear Reaction". *Nature* 143, 239. [doi:10.1038/143239a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/143239a0)

name: Rutherford scattering and discovery of the nucleus
summary: Rutherford's 1911 analysis of alpha scattering revealed the nucleus and founded both nuclear physics and the scattering method that runs through particle and condensed-matter physics.
sources: Rutherford (1911). "The Scattering of α and β Particles by Matter and the Structure of the Atom". *Phil. Mag.* 21, 669. [doi:10.1080/14786440508637080](https://doi.org/10.1080/14786440508637080)

name: Nuclear EFT as a case study of levels and emergence
summary: Chiral EFT is a worked example in philosophy of physics of how autonomous effective levels relate to a deeper theory: nuclear physics is derivable from QCD in principle yet is organized by its own degrees of freedom, power counting and low-energy constants.
breaks: Philosophical readings (autonomy versus reduction) differ, and the derivation from QCD is only partial via lattice matching.
sources: Weinberg (1990). "Nuclear forces from chiral lagrangians". *Phys. Lett. B* 251, 288. [doi:10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3](https://doi.org/10.1016/0370-2693(90)90938-3)

name: Resonances as S-matrix poles and Coulomb functions
summary: Nuclear resonances are poles of the S-matrix on the unphysical sheet (Breit-Wigner, R-matrix, Gamow states), and charged-particle reactions and alpha decay use Coulomb wave functions and the Gamow factor from the analytic structure of the Coulomb problem.
breaks: Threshold effects and overlapping resonances make pole extraction model-dependent.
sources: Lane & Thomas (1958). "R-Matrix Theory of Nuclear Reactions". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 30, 257. [doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.30.257](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.30.257)

name: Self-consistent Green's functions and optical potentials
summary: The self-consistent Green's function method computes nuclear spectral functions from Dyson's equation, and its self-energy is a microscopic nucleon-nucleus optical potential, uniting structure and reaction theory with propagator mathematics.
map: G=G^0+G^0\Sigma^\star G,\ \Sigma^\star(\mathbf r,\mathbf r';E)\leftrightarrow U_{\rm opt}(E);\ S(k,E)=-\tfrac1\pi\mathrm{Im}G
breaks: Truncations (ADC(n)) and three-body forces limit accuracy, and the optical potential's imaginary part needs a large model space.
sources: Dickhoff & Barbieri (2004). "Self-consistent Green's function method for nuclei and nuclear matter". *Prog. Part. Nucl. Phys.* 52, 377. [arXiv:nucl-th/0402034](https://arxiv.org/abs/nucl-th/0402034)

name: Shared detector electronics and noise limits
summary: Nuclear spectroscopy defined the charge-sensitive preamplifier, pulse shaping, photomultiplier and SiPM readout and the Fano and series/parallel noise analysis now generic to instrumentation.
breaks: Optimal shaping depends on detector capacitance and leakage; the noise model is generic but parameters are detector-specific.
sources: Fano (1947). "Ionization Yield of Radiations. II. The Fluctuations of the Number of Ions". *Phys. Rev.* 72, 26. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.72.26](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.72.26)
